_rule: Copy these strings EXACTLY. Never paraphrase, reword, shorten, or improvise camera language. The test: does this exact string exist below? If it is your own wording, delete it and paste the library string. Applies equally to Stage 2 base image prompts, Stage 3 Kling shot boxes, and Stage 4 Seedance shot lists.
_variation_rule: Never repeat the same camera angle or shot size as the shot immediately before it. Close Up, Medium Shot, Close Up is valid. Close Up, Close Up is never valid. This holds even on 'minimal switching' - that setting changes how OFTEN you cut, not whether the angle changes when you do.

shot_size.name: Establishing Shot
shot_size.use_when: The scene is about the full place, geography, or where everybody is positioned.

shot_size.name: Extreme Wide Shot
shot_size.string: Wide shot of subject while showing the entire location in the frame.
shot_size.use_when: Showing body language against a big location.

shot_size.name: Wide Shot
shot_size.use_when: The subject matters but the environment still needs to be seen.

shot_size.name: Medium Shot
shot_size.use_when: Performance, dialogue, body language, readable emotion.

shot_size.name: Extreme Close Up
shot_size.use_when: What the subject feels internally, not what they do physically.

shot_size.name: Close Up
shot_size.use_when: Face, emotion, reaction, or one important detail.

shot_size.name: Detail Shot
shot_size.use_when: A small object, body part, clue, screen, hand, or action detail.

angle.name: Medium Low Angle
angle.string: Low Angle, Camera looking up at the subject
angle.use_when: The subject should feel powerful, threatening, heroic, or dominant.

angle.name: High Angle Top Down View
angle.use_when: Looking down on the scene, seeing placement clearly.

angle.name: High Angle Top Down Foreshortening
angle.string: High Angle Top down view, exaggerated foreshortening, head appears big in the foreground torso in the mid ground medium size, waist shrinks down the body in the background

angle.name: Low Angle Foreshortening (1/5)
angle.string: Focus distance: Extremely close, focused on foreground
angle.use_when: Strong low-angle body distortion from the ground upward.

angle.name: Low Angle Foreshortening (2/5)
angle.string: Camera angle relative to subject: Extreme low angle, worm's-eye view looking straight up
angle.use_when: part of the Low Angle Foreshortening block - paste all five lines together

angle.name: Low Angle Foreshortening (3/5)
angle.use_when: part of the Low Angle Foreshortening block - paste all five lines together

angle.name: Low Angle Foreshortening (4/5)
angle.string: Head, Torso, Bottom size as they appear in the frame: Head is positioned at the top center and appears small; Torso is positioned in the middle center and appears medium; Bottom and feet are positioned at the bottom center, occupying the lower half, appearing extremely large
angle.use_when: part of the Low Angle Foreshortening block - paste all five lines together

angle.name: Low Angle Foreshortening (5/5)
angle.string: Subject Foreshortening: Highly exaggerated; feet are closest to the camera, legs extend into the midground, torso and head are furthest away
angle.use_when: part of the Low Angle Foreshortening block - paste all five lines together

angle.name: High Angle Top Down Drone Shot
angle.string: High Angle Top down Drone Shot, the entire location is visible in the frame, subject appear small in the frame
angle.use_when: The entire location or area must be visible.

angle.name: POV shot
angle.string: POV shot. Only hands are visible

angle.name: Dutch Angle
angle.string: Dutch angle shot, camera tilted diagonally, horizon line slanted, subject framed off-balance
angle.use_when: Unstable, wrong, threatening, surreal, emotionally disturbed.

character_view.name: Rear Back View
character_view.string: rear back view, back is visible

blocking.name: Over the Shoulder
blocking.string: Over the shoulder shot of character [Subject X], back is visible, in front of them is [Subject X]

blocking.name: Over the Hip
blocking.string: Over the hip shot of character [Subject X], back is visible, in front of them is [Subject X]
blocking.use_when: Body movement, hands, objects, weapons, walking, tension, revealing something lower in frame.

blocking.name: Triangle - 2 Foreground, 1 Background
blocking.string: Triangle shot of [Subject 1] and [Subject 2] in the foreground, backs are visible. In front of them is [Subject 3] [Subject 3's Character view]

blocking.name: Triangle - 1 Foreground, 2 Background
blocking.string: Triangle shot of [Subject 1] in the foreground, backs is visible, in front of them is [Subject 2] [Subject 2's Character view] and [Subject 2] [Subject 2's Character view]

blocking.name: Face to Face
blocking.string: Face to Face side profile views

_slash_rule: For a slash pair like 'Camera Pans Down / Up', use only the direction the shot needs. For blocking strings with [Subject X] placeholders, fill the names and keep every other word identical.

camera_feel._note: Seedance header 'Camera feel:' line. The VALUE is the exact library movement string.
camera_feel.mix_rule: Handheld for tense, emotional or action-driven generations. Static for product reveals, composed emotional close-ups, deliberate framing.

seedance_always_include: NO MUSIC, only natural ambient sounds.
No texts or subtitles on screen.

global_setup.handheld: Handheld camera throughout. No music, only SFX and natural ambience.
global_setup.static: Static camera throughout. No music, only SFX and natural ambience.

kling_boilerplate.ending: The subject stops talking, silence in the room.

_ip_rule: director.md bans referencing existing IP anywhere in any prompt, but the mandated verbatim tone strings name films and cinematographers. The Visual tone line is the one exemption. Any IP check must skip it.

_guide_extras._note: From the guide's Camera Work chapter, NOT from the director instruction's camera language library. The director names six categories that require an exact library string and subject placement is not among them. Use these as framing vocabulary when composing a base image; do not treat them as sanctioned library strings and do not rely on them to satisfy the exact-camera-string rule.
